title: Raise the source_id capture bound from 8 s to 30 s in TermAl (S0, after-capture, engram source invocation)
outcome: Every TermAl budget that bounds a source_id capture (the native S0 capture, the after-run capture, the received-notice capture and the `engram source` invocation with its --timeout-ms) allows 30 s instead of 8 s. The S0 opening deadline leaves room for a 30 s capture plus the existing opening stages. Budgets that do not bound a source_id capture are unchanged. Engram's `engram source` accepts 30 s in the same window.
acceptance: Every TermAl budget that bounds a source_id capture allows 30 s: the S0 capture, the after-run capture, the received-notice capture, the `engram source` subprocess budget, and the --timeout-ms value it passes (no longer capped at 8000). The S0 opening deadline allows such a capture plus the existing opening stages. Budgets unrelated to source_id capture are unchanged, and the change lists each site touched or deliberately left alone.

Behaviour tests show that a capture taking longer than 8 s and under 30 s is accepted, and that one exceeding 30 s still yields unavailable with no credit. Existing tests that pin 8 s are updated to the new bound, not removed. No test reads Markdown or instruction files.

The change lands under the standing rule (review pair, FULL on Windows and DL560), is installed, and runs after a TermAl restart. The paired Engram change (the `engram source` bound to 30 s) is landed and installed before or with it, so the two agree.

completion.summary: Shared30s source_id bound delivered in landed/installed/running TermAl30ddf016 with pairedEngramfc749042; coordinator confirms C1-C3 and realconsumercredit.
